final_message:
I fixed the bug: a coupon with `max_redemptions=1` was still redeemable after its one redemption, so the second `subscribe` went through.

The cause was an off-by-one in `is_redeemable` in `billing/discounts.py`. It rejected a coupon only when `times_redeemed > max_redemptions`, so an exhausted coupon still passed. I changed `>` to `>=`.

The suite passes (24 tests). I only ran the existing tests: your reproduction test isn't in the suite, so it hasn't been run. I also didn't run mypy.

I wrote `answer.json` in the repository root: `{"file": "discounts.py", "function": "is_redeemable"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && grep -n "redemption\|def " discounts.py | head -60; grep -n "coupon" engine.py | head -40
cd billing && sed -n 60,90p discounts.py; grep -n "coupon" subscriptions.py

sed -i 's/coupon\["times_redeemed"\] > coupon\["max_redemptions"\]/coupon["times_redeemed"] >= coupon["max_redemptions"]/' discounts.py && cd .. && echo '{"file": "discounts.py", "function": "is_redeemable"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

pwd; sed -i '' 's/coupon\["times_redeemed"\] > coupon/coupon["times_redeemed"] >= coupon/' discounts.py && cd .. && echo '{"file": "discounts.py", "function": "is_redeemable"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
